hypothesis: A loader-consumption label plus pre-load digest is insufficient evidence that the loader actually received the exact admitted bytes. A producer-side immutable byte handoff can close that source-level evidence gap before any model-runtime promotion.
counterhypothesis: A sealed-byte adapter could still be cosmetic if the real model loader ignores the supplied byte argument or if the downstream registry accepts a caller-forged witness. Therefore this primitive is source/test evidence only and requires binding to a real loader implementation plus canonical external admission before runtime credit.

mechanism: create anonymous Linux memfd with MFD_ALLOW_SEALING
read and SHA-256 verify exact sealed bytes
supply those bytes to one explicitly bound loader callable
re-read seals and digest after the loader returns
emit candidate witness material for downstream canonical loader-consumption admission
delta.authority_boundary: WITNESS_IS_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE_ONLY; IT DOES_NOT_MINT_CANONICAL_STATE, MODEL_EXECUTION, JSPACE_CAUSALITY, OR TRAINING_CREDIT

obligations: exact sealed bytes are supplied to the bound loader
mutable caller input is snapshotted before load
invalid loader-binding digest fails before loader call
loader exception produces no false witness

external_mechanism_basis.python_fcntl: Python 3.13 documents F_ADD_SEALS/F_GET_SEALS and F_SEAL_* for os.memfd_create-backed descriptors.
external_mechanism_basis.python_os: Python 3.13 documents os.memfd_create and MFD_ALLOW_SEALING on supported Linux platforms.
external_mechanism_basis.linux_memfd: Linux memfd_create provides an anonymous memory-backed file and sealing controls that can prevent writes/grow/shrink and further seal changes.
